channel.title: Bollam Rishithej — Writing
channel.description: Notes on deep technology, company building and corporate governance.

item.title: Some of India's best technology is already here. It's sitting in a university lab
item.description: A visit to the MEMS, Microfluidics and Nanoelectronics Lab at BITS Pilani Hyderabad, and why VidyuthLabs would rather commercialise research that already exists than reinvent it.

item.title: Fifty thousand people
item.description: The number I care about is not valuation or revenue. It is how many families have a salary because something we built exists. The target is fifty thousand in ten years.

item.title: The one-office rule, and what it does to a founder's board map
item.description: Section 203 of the Companies Act lets a person hold exactly one whole-time key managerial office. That single constraint shapes how a multi-company founder is allowed to sign.

item.title: Start with one school
item.description: How we enter an unorganised sector — find one partner willing to run it for real, build for their actual constraints, and only then call it a product. In education that partner is Deccan Springs Global School.

item.title: We don't have competitors
item.description: The competitive frame is the default in Indian startup culture and I think it is largely a mistake. In an unorganised market the constraint is never the other company. It is that the sector does not work yet.
